issues.description: HAS_PERCENTAGE regex is case-sensitive but keyframe selectors `from`/`to` can be uppercase
issues.detail: The other regex `HAS_KEYWORD` carries the `i` flag, but `HAS_PERCENTAGE` does not. Percentage selectors are digits+%, so that's fine, but the symmetry hides a real risk: any future addition of a letter token to PERCENTAGE_SELECTORS silently drops uppercase matches. Either document why no `i` flag, or just add it. The maintainer six years from now will trip on this.

issues.description: import-notation `url` branch skips params containing `url(` instead of requiring them
issues.detail: `if (primary === 'url' && /url\(/i.test(params)) return;` exits early when params DO contain `url(` — which is exactly the case the rule needs to validate when enforcing `url` notation (to flag strings that should be wrapped). The inverted condition looks wrong on its face. Either there's a test gap or the logic is backwards; show me the failing test that proves I'm wrong.

issues.description: HAS_NUMERIC built from Map keys is fine but `\b` won't anchor digit-only tokens cleanly against `.`
issues.detail: `\b(?:100|200|...)\b` matches inside `1000` partially? No — `\b` between `0` and `0` is not a word boundary, so `1000` won't match `100`. Good. But `100.5` will match `100` since `.` is a non-word char. Probably harmless for font-weight values, but worth a comment or a stricter anchor. Cheap to make robust now.

issues.description: Six prefilter regexes built inline, no shared helper, no benchmark numbers in commit
issues.detail: The PR claims a performance fix but the changeset entry is one line and there are no before/after numbers in the description. For a perf patch that touches six rules, show the measurement. Otherwise the next person tuning these has no baseline to compare against and may undo the work thinking it's dead code.

issues.description: Selector prefilter `/:/ ` will match attribute selectors like `[href*=":"]` and pass through unnecessarily
issues.detail: Not a bug — the inner code still does the right thing — but the prefilter is weaker than it could be. `/::?[a-z]/i` would screen out attribute-selector noise without missing real pseudo-elements. Minor. The current form is honest and obvious; the tighter form is faster but less readable. Author's call.

issues.description: Good taste: removing the redundant `selector.includes(':not(')` check by pushing it into walkRules filter
issues.detail: This is the right shape. The old code did the check twice — once as walk filter convention, once inline. Moving it into the walkRules regex argument eliminates the special case and matches the pattern used by the other selector-* rules. GOOD-TASTE. Noting it so the next reviewer understands why this part of the diff is unobjectionable.

review.summary: NEEDS-WORK. The patch shape is right — push cheap string/regex prefilters in front of expensive parsers, and consolidate the walkRules filter to match the pattern other selector-* rules already use. That's good taste. But one branch reads backwards (import-notation `url` returns early on the matching case, which is the opposite of what the other branches do), one regex lacks the `i` flag its sibling has, and a perf PR with no numbers in the commit message is a perf PR that the next maintainer can't defend. Fix the inverted condition, prove it with a test, add the measurement to the changeset, and this lands.
